title: CLO Tips Workshop - Custom Button UV Map
description: Quickly add the finishing touch to your design! Follow CLO technical experts to use custom button UV maps!
transcript:
See this picture.  
It is a round button.  
There are two holes in the middle.  
What about this kind of button?  
There is one in CLO.  
We see the window of this picture book.  
Subtract.  
Here I will switch to list view.  
Find the button and the button eye file.  
Open the button.  
Among these buttons,  
find two round buttons that meet our needs.  
Switch to icon view,  
which makes it convenient for us to look at the search chart,  
just like this.  
Hover the mouse over the button and a number appears:  
a line button 9.  
Remember this number.  
Then go up,  
find the UV document folder,  
double click to open.  
In any document,  
right-click on the document,  
copy the path.  
Open the file,  
then paste and go to the path.  
There are many PSD files here.  
These are the standard files that CLO has prepared for you.  
We just need to follow the instructions,  
and you can do the UV texture step by step.  
Open Photoshop (PS).  
A line button 9,  
drag it to PS to open.  
After opening, we can see the drawing.  
According to this color, several areas are divided,  
and there is corresponding text on it as a reminder.  
The largest area on the top is the front of the button,  
the bottom is the back,  
and the upper right corner is the side of the button eye.  
Because there are two buttons,  
there are two small lines here.  
The text is in Chinese, English, and Korean.  
We can keep only the Chinese text.  
On the right layer panel,  
hide the other two languages,  
show only Chinese.  
Drag the button drawing in.  
Use the left mouse button,  
the left mouse button can drag directly.  
Place it on the back here first.  
Pull the empty square of the grid,  
you can zoom in.  
Zoom in and take a closer look.  
Place the picture next to it,  
take a closer look.  
We have to ensure that this twisted texture  
can cover the bottom.  
This green circle  
can be slightly larger,  
basically covered.  
Then click on this checkmark above.  
Right-click on the layer,  
convert to smart object.  
The eyes of these two lines are vertical.  
Select the layer,  
press CTRL plus K.  
At this time, you can adjust the size, shape, angle, etc.  
Rotate it to a vertical position.  
Then click on this checkmark above.  
We still need to adjust the eyes of the two lines,  
because the size and position of these two eyes  
actually do not necessarily match  
the two eyes on the bottom board.  
So to ensure  
there is no difference in the twisted texture,  
we need to adjust these two eyes.  
Hide it,  
turn it into  
vertical texture around.  
Use the transform tool,  
rotate it up.  
At this time, a selection will be generated.  
Fill other patterns into this selection.  
The shortcut key is Shift plus F5.  
Select Content-Aware Fill, confirm.  
Repeat the previous operation once more:  
Shift plus F5,  
select Content-Aware Fill,  
confirm.  
It will be processed shortly.  
Copy the twisted texture to one.  
CTRL plus C, CTRL plus V.  
Not yet.  
Here I want to remind everyone,  
although this place only shows the front,  
in fact this area,  
its texture is not only the front,  
there is also a circle which is the side texture of this twist.  
Zoom in a little.  
This place has several circles,  
this white line,  
the white line on the outside,  
to the middle of the green line.  
This section of the range  
is the side texture of the twist.  
Drag the twisted texture over.  
If the texture is not big enough,  
let's adjust it again,  
still CTRL plus T,  
a little bigger,  
then use the arrow keys on the keyboard  
to make slight movements.  
Click to match, use the arrow keys on the keyboard,  
click the button to align.  
After placing the number,  
let's do the side texture.  
The side of the twist is pure white.  
Make a large circle directly,  
just fill the circle with white.  
Select the twisted texture,  
copy it with CTRL plus J,  
place this layer below.  
Still use CTRL plus T to resize the circle,  
can be slightly larger than the green circle.  
Click to confirm.  
Press the CTRL key at the same time,  
left mouse button,  
press on the layer to shrink,  
then press Shift plus F5,  
select white,  
CTRL plus D to deselect.  
Next, deal with the side of the twist.  
Switch to the rectangular marquee tool,  
select all the squares on the side of the twist,  
Shift plus F5 fill with white.  
That's it.  
Then save it as a JPG picture.  
Before saving, you can hide other layers.  
Select the save location,  
choose JPG format,  
select the quality you need.  
Here the selection is the highest quality.  
Finally, click to confirm.  
Return to the software.  
Next, on this style,  
use our new twist,  
add a twist,  
wait a moment.  
Then in the shape section here,  
find the two-eyed round twist we chose at the beginning,  
continue to look down.  
There is a text here,  
and a corresponding browse button next to it.  
Click to add the picture just now to it,  
wait a moment.  
I still can't see the twist effect.  
You need to add the twist to this garment first.  
Switch to the move twist tool,  
select all five twists on the front,  
press Shift to select multiple,  
find the apply button on the right side of the new twist.  
You can see the effect in the 3D window.  
This twist should be:  
the purple part on top,  
the white part below.  
That is to say,  
the twist should rotate 90 degrees counterclockwise.  
Select all twists,  
there is an angle setting in the property editor,  
change it to 90.  
Complete.

chunks.title: CLO Tips Workshop - Custom Button UV Map
chunks.content: ## Overview of Custom Button UV Mapping in CLO This section explains the process of creating and applying a custom UV map texture for a round button with two holes in CLO. It covers locating button assets, editing UV maps in Photoshop, preparing textures, and applying them correctly within CLO to achieve accurate 3D button visualization. --- ## Locating and Preparing Button Assets in CLO This section details how to find and identify the appropriate button and UV map files within CLO’s asset directories, including navigating the button library and UV document folders. - Identify the target button: a round button with two holes. - Switch CLO’s view to **list view** to locate the button and its related files. - Switch to **icon view** for easier visual search. - Hover over buttons to display their reference number (e.g., “line button 9”). - Note the button number for use in UV mapping. - Open the **UV document folder** within CLO’s directory. - Right-click on a UV map document to copy its path. - Open the folder externally to access many **PSD files** CLO provides as standard UV templates. - These PSD files guide step-by-step UV texture creation for buttons. --- ## Editing the Button UV Map in Photoshop This section explains how to open, interpret, and modify the UV map PSD file for the button in Photoshop, including managing layers and preparing the texture for CLO. - Open Photoshop (PS). - Drag the identified button PSD file (e.g., “line button 9”) into Photoshop. - The PSD contains a segmented drawing with color-coded areas representing: - **Front of the button** (largest area on top) - **Back of the button** (bottom area) - **Side of the button eye** (upper right corner) - The PSD includes text labels in Chinese, English, and Korean; hide all but the Chinese layer for clarity. - Import the custom button texture by dragging it into Photoshop. - Use the left mouse button to drag and position the texture layer onto the back area of the UV map. - Zoom in to align the texture precisely over the grid’s empty square. - The green circle boundary on the UV map indicates the texture coverage area for the button’s back. - Confirm placement by clicking the checkmark. - Convert the texture layer to a **Smart Object** (right-click layer → Convert to Smart Object). - Use **Ctrl + K** to transform the texture layer (resize, rotate, skew). - Rotate the two vertical “eyes” (button holes) to match the vertical orientation on the UV map. - Confirm transformations. --- ## Adjusting Button Eye Textures and Filling Areas This section covers detailed adjustments to the button eye areas and filling unwanted texture parts using Photoshop’s Content-Aware Fill. - The two button eye holes may not exactly match the UV map holes in size or position. - Adjust their position and size using Photoshop’s transform tools. - Rotate the eye textures vertically to match the UV map’s orientation.

chunks.title: CLO Tips Workshop - Custom Button UV Map
chunks.content: - Rotate the two vertical “eyes” (button holes) to match the vertical orientation on the UV map. - Confirm transformations. --- ## Adjusting Button Eye Textures and Filling Areas This section covers detailed adjustments to the button eye areas and filling unwanted texture parts using Photoshop’s Content-Aware Fill. - The two button eye holes may not exactly match the UV map holes in size or position. - Adjust their position and size using Photoshop’s transform tools. - Rotate the eye textures vertically to match the UV map’s orientation. - Use the **rectangular marquee tool** to select areas around the eyes. - Press **Shift + F5** and choose **Content-Aware Fill** to fill unwanted parts with surrounding texture. - Repeat Content-Aware Fill as needed to clean the texture. - Copy the twisted texture area with **Ctrl + C** and paste it (**Ctrl + V**) to duplicate if necessary. --- ## Incorporating the Side Texture of the Button Twist This section explains how to handle the side texture of the button twist, which appears around the button’s edge. - The button’s texture is not only the front but also includes the **side texture** represented by circular areas on the UV map. - The side texture is indicated by white lines between the outer and inner green circles. - Drag the twisted texture to cover the side circle area. - Adjust size with **Ctrl + T** (transform) to ensure the side texture completely covers the UV side circle. - Use arrow keys for fine alignment. - The side of the twist is pure white. - Fill the side circle with white by creating a large white-filled circle using Photoshop’s tools. - Duplicate the twisted texture layer (**Ctrl + J**) and place it below. - Resize the duplicated layer slightly larger than the green circle. - Use **Shift + F5** with white fill to clean unwanted areas on the duplicated layer. - Use the rectangular marquee tool to select the side squares of the twist area on the UV map. - Fill these side squares with white using **Shift + F5**. --- ## Saving the Finished UV Texture and Applying it in CLO This section outlines saving the completed UV texture as a JPG and applying it to the button twist in CLO to visualize the effect correctly. - Hide unnecessary layers before saving. - Save the file as a **JPG** in the desired location. - Choose the highest quality setting for best results. - Return to CLO software. - In the style properties, add a new twist and select the two-eyed round twist button identified earlier. - Click the browse button to add the newly saved JPG texture. - Initially, the twist effect might not be visible. - Ensure the twist is applied to the garment by using the **move twist tool**. - Select all front twists (use Shift to multi-select). - Click the **apply button** on the new twist to see the effect in the 3D window.

chunks.title: CLO Tips Workshop - Custom Button UV Map
chunks.content: - In the style properties, add a new twist and select the two-eyed round twist button identified earlier. - Click the browse button to add the newly saved JPG texture. - Initially, the twist effect might not be visible. - Ensure the twist is applied to the garment by using the **move twist tool**. - Select all front twists (use Shift to multi-select). - Click the **apply button** on the new twist to see the effect in the 3D window. - The twist texture should appear with the purple part on top and white part below. - Rotate the twist 90 degrees counterclockwise by setting the angle to 90 in the property editor. - Confirm the twist angle to complete the setup. --- ## Summary This workflow enables creating precise UV texture maps for custom buttons in CLO using Photoshop. It includes locating assets, editing UV maps with smart objects and content-aware fills, correctly covering front, back, and side textures, saving optimized JPG files, and applying the textures with proper orientation in CLO’s 3D environment. This process ensures accurate and visually consistent button textures on garments.
